newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stock markets extend recent losses.
newsitem.headline: Asian stock markets extend recent losses.

text.p: Most Asian markets ended Tuesday flat or weaker on a range of local factors, the exception being in Manila, where the market defied gloomy forecasts to jump nearly two percent.

The Philippine Stock Exchange index finished up on a technical rebound from Monday's 3.73 percent drop. The main index closed Tuesday at 2,904.41, up 52.25 points or 1.83 percent as bargain-hunters snapped up oversold issues, brokers said.
Tuesday's surge surprised analysts, who had predicted the market would continue to lose ground. But they said the market would likely consolidate on Wednesday and test the 2,850-point support level.
The rest of Asia saw a continuation of the gloom that has seized regional bourses in recent days.
Tokyo stocks managed only slight gains on buying of export-related shares expected to benefit from the yen's weakness, brokers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 index settled at 20,958.08, up 72.67 points or 0.35 percent.
"But the Nikkei average is still basically stuck in a box range," said Kenzo Doi, a strategist at Kokusai Securities.

In Hong Kong, stocks slid due to profit-taking in leading shares and some futures-related activity, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index finished down 70.6 points, or 0.58 percent, to close at 12,192.17.
The finance sector led the index down, chiefly sell-offs in HSBC Holdings and Hang Seng Bank.
"I wouldn't expect this round of profit-taking to be too extended," said Conal Sanjana, institutional sales manager at Kerry Securities. "
Seoul stocks closed sharply lower on fears of a glut of shares next month, brokers said. The market fell 13.76 points, or 1.76 percent, to a provisional close of 766.32.
"Everyone is getting more and more nervous," said Seung-wook Choe of Schroders Securities.
An estimated 700 billion to 1.2 trillion won worth of new shares are coming into the market in November from initial public offerings and rights issues.
Taiwan's stock index tumbled 65.05 points or 1.01 percent to end the session at 6,359.67 as the market's recent sluggishness prompted investors to transfer funds elsewhere, brokers said.
Thai stocks declined for the fourth straight day on weak sentiment stemming from market rumours that some property developers faced cash-flow problems, brokers said.
The SET index moved in a negative zone throughout the session and closed 6.95 points, or 0.75 percent, lower at 924.56. The SET-50 index dropped 0.57 point to 69.65.

Australian shares drifted down to end near their lows on the day as investors showed caution ahead of the release of key U.S. economic data this week and after the Dow and base metals prices softened on Monday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed down 11.1 points at 2,323.0, a decline of 0.48 percent.
New Zealand's NZSE-40 capital index dropped 32.72 points or 1.41 percent to 2,294.48, compounding a one percent slump in the previous session last Friday.
Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index closed flat at 2,061.98, down 5.87 points or 0.28 percent.

The U.S. dollar, which has traded at 42-month highs the past two days, retreated slightly in Tokyo trading on Tuesday after breaking the 115-yen barrier earlier in the day. At 1115 GMT, the dollar was trading at 113.81/13.94 yen and 1.5123/27 marks.
Bullion ended at US$382.50/383.00 an ounce in Hong Kong, against New York's Monday close of US$382.90/383.40.

In Singapore, North Sea Brent December crude oil futures fell on news that U.S. lawmakers didn't expect the United States would face a heating-oil crunch this winter. December ended at $24.02 per barrel.
